title: anywaye service manifest
description: Schema for anywaye.yml, the per-service manifest every anywaye repository carries. A manifest is the one place that declares what a thing IS (service or template), its identity, its core spec constraint, the contract surface it exposes and consumes, where each dependency runs per environment, and who owns it. Cross-field rules that JSON Schema cannot express (a published event type must be prefixed by the publishing service; a service never consumes its own events; a consumed type must exist in the core catalog; exposes.api is required for any service that serves traffic; a template declares no events and names a generator instead) are documented in docs/manifest-conventions.md and enforced by tests/test_specs.py.

kind.description: What this entry IS. `service` is a running thing that is resolved, deployed and called. `template` is a thing consumed at GENERATE time: `caf init` renders it and the caller owns the output, so it is versioned and pinned in a registry exactly like a service but is never a running process. Defaults to `service`, so an existing manifest that omits it means what it always meant. A template declares no events and no api, because it has no runtime contract to break.

name.description: The anywaye namespace name. Also the repository name and the value used as the event envelope `source`.

description.description: One sentence on what the service is for. Shown by `caf new` and by pantry.

language.description: Implementation language, or `spec` for specification-only repositories (core itself, contract-test fixtures).

core.description: Constraint on the core spec version this service was written against, e.g. ^0.1.0. Service CI pins core to a release inside this range.

environments.description: Where each dependency runs, per environment. This is the ONLY place self-host-vs-hosted is expressed, and it is a declaration of intent rather than a runtime flag: one manifest says it once, and `cafe dev`, `caf deploy` and CI all read the same answer. The `default` environment applies wherever no named environment matches, so a single-environment project needs no block at all. An absent dependency is self-hosted, because the default posture of the platform is that you own what you declare.

env.description: Environment variables this service needs at runtime. The single source of truth for configuration: name, whether it is required, whether it is a secret, and its default. `anywaye` generates .env.example, boot validators, and docs/configuration.md from this list. Secret values never appear here — only names and metadata.

required.description: Whether the service refuses to boot without it.

secret.description: Whether the value is a secret. Secrets are never printed, logged, or committed; their values live in the keyring (dev) or k8s Secrets (prod).

default.description: Default value for non-secret config. Omit for secrets (they are provisioned, not defaulted).

dev_default.description: Default for local dev. Use 'auto' to have cafe generate a dev value on first run.

description.description: One sentence on what this variable is for.

exposes.description: The contract surface this service publishes. Omit entirely for libraries, specification-only repositories and templates; a service that serves or receives traffic must declare at least one of api/events.

api.description: Repository-relative path to the OpenAPI 3.1 document describing the HTTP surface.

events.description: Event types this service publishes, as <service>.<entity>.<action>. The first segment must be this manifest's own `name`; see docs/event-naming.md.

consumes.description: Event types this service subscribes to, as <service>.<entity>.<action>. The prefix names the publisher, which is never this service. Delivery is at-least-once, so every consumer must be idempotent.

dependencies.description: Other anywaye services this service builds on. Sync dependencies, not a package manager.

x-anywaye-reserved-properties.description: TOMBSTONED PROPERTY NAMES. The names this service has removed from its contract and will never publish again, each with the contract surface it used to live on. This is an EXTENSION POINT: the `x-anywaye-` prefix is core's reserved namespace for manifest keys that carry no runtime meaning and exist only so a rule has something to read, and a key outside that prefix is rejected by `additionalProperties: false` rather than silently ignored. THE HAZARD IT EXISTS FOR IS NAME REUSE. If a service publishes `invoice_id`, a consumer generates source against it, the service deletes the field, and an unrelated field later wants the same name, the consumer that upgrades its generated source binds to the NEW field under the OLD name and nothing errors anywhere. Tombstoning the name is the whole mechanism: the name stays reserved, and a later document that reintroduces it is a failure rather than a coincidence. WHY EACH ENTRY CARRIES `was`: a bare list of names cannot say whether a name was ever published. A tombstone for a name this service never exposed blocks a legitimate future field forever and reports nothing while it does, because the rule that would have caught it has nothing to compare against — so the name is declared together with the surface it was removed from, and a reservation that points at a surface this service does not publish is a stale entry rather than a promise. ENFORCED BY `harness/reserved_check.py`, which is the only code that reads this key; see `harness/breaking_tiers.json`'s `reserved-no-delete` row and `docs/reserved-properties.md`.

serviceName.description: anywaye namespace rule: lowercase kebab-case, starting with a letter, no trailing separator. 2-40 characters. Reserved: anywaye, caf, kit, core.

provisioning.description: WHERE a dependency runs. `self-hosted` means the caller runs it, in their own compose, on their own machines, with no anywaye account involved. `hosted` means anywaye runs it and the caller consumes it over the network. This is the switch your ethos names — build once, deploy once, use everywhere — and it is declared once, per environment, rather than being discovered at runtime.

environmentResolution.description: Where each of this service's dependencies runs in one environment. Every key is a dependency from `dependencies`; an omitted dependency is self-hosted.

eventType.description: Event type: <service>.<entity>.<action>, exactly three segments. The first segment is a anywaye service name (kebab-case) and must be the publishing service's own `name`; the entity and action segments are lowercase snake_case. See docs/event-naming.md.

semverRange.description: anywaye semver constraint: ^MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, ~MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, >=MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, or an exact MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Prereleases are out of scope for v0.

openapiRef.description: Repository-relative path to an OpenAPI 3.1 document (.yaml, .yml or .json). No leading ./, no absolute paths, no URLs.

version.description: Constraint on the dependency's own contract version.

required.description: false marks a soft dependency: the service runs without it, degraded.

url.description: SSH remote only. HTTPS remotes for anywaye/anywaye repos are a policy violation (PLAN.md §1).

propertyName.description: An OpenAPI property name: lowercase snake_case, starting with a letter. The same grammar the event payload schemas under schemas/events/ use for their `properties` keys, because a reserved name is a payload property name and a tombstone that could not have been published is a tombstone for nothing. Deliberately NOT a name that merely parses: the point of the tombstone is that the exact string is what a consumer's generated source still carries, so the reservation has to be the string itself.

contractSurface.description: Where a property used to live, as `<service>.<entity>.<action>` for an event payload or `path/to/schemas/<Name>.schema.json` for an OpenAPI components schema. A reservation must name the surface it protects, because a name with no surface is a name nobody can tell was ever published, and the check that would catch a stale entry has nothing to compare against. The event-type form is the same three-segment grammar as everywhere else in core, so one pattern decides it.

reservedProperty.description: One tombstoned property name and the contract surface it was removed from. Two fields and no others: a name is what stays reserved, and a surface is what makes the reservation checkable in both directions — a name live in a document is a reuse, and a name attached to no surface this service publishes is a stale entry that will block a legitimate future field forever.

note.description: Why the property was removed and where a consumer gets the data now. Optional because the decision is not the manifest's to record; useful because the reader of a tombstone six releases later is trying to find out whether the removal was a mistake.

team.description: Owning team in the anywaye namespace.

contact.description: Reachable mailbox for contract and incident questions.
